result.rationale: The diff changes calendar references to arrays (calendarReference = references.filter(...)) and creates one reference per destination calendar in createAllCalendarEvents, so collective bookings now carry multiple _calendar references. However the merge/reschedule deletion path still uses a single `find`: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` — deleting only the first match and orphaning remaining hosts' events when merging. The mechanism is visible in the diff and consistent with the new multi-reference behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, calendar references were updated from a single `find` to `filter` + loop (so multiple `_calendar` refs are generally handled). However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId) { ... }`) it still deletes only one old calendar event via `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`. With destination calendars now supporting multiple per-host references, this `find` will delete only the first matched calendar reference, potentially leaving other hosts’ old calendar events orphaned after a merge/reschedule scenario that triggers this block.
